driverWhy.growth: FY26 = 2026 guidance EUR 43-45bn (Q2-26). FY27 reflects record backlog and AI-driven capacity adds, then growth fades to ~5% as the cycle normalises. Base FY30 revenue sits just above the 2030 range of EUR 44-60bn because FY26 already exceeds its low end.
driverWhy.gm: FY26 guide 54-56%. Base trends to 57%, inside ASML's 2030 target band of 56-60% (EUV mix, High-NA maturing, services).
driverWhy.ebitda_m: FY25A 37.7%, H1-26 op. margin 36.6% with H2 guided higher. Opex (R&D ~14% of sales) grows slower than revenue = operating leverage. Bear shows a downturn with R&D held flat in absolute terms.
driverWhy.da_pct: FY21-25 range 2.5-3.3%, FY25 3.1%. The new capacity build-out lifts the absolute D&A level.
driverWhy.capex_pct: FY21-25 average 6.4% (peak 8.0% in FY23 capacity expansion, 5.0% in FY25). Base 5.5% as capex normalises but EUV/High-NA capacity is still added.
driverWhy.nwc_pct: ASML runs negative NWC because customers pay EUV down payments (contract liabilities). It was -27% in FY25 but fell to about -7% of LTM sales by Jun-26 as down payments were consumed. Base normalises to -12%, below the FY21-25 average.
driverWhy.tax: Effective tax rate FY21-25 15.0-18.6% (Dutch innovation box), FY25 17.7%. Pillar Two 15% minimum is not binding.
driverWhy.g: Long-run nominal growth: euro-area inflation ~2% + modest real growth in semiconductor content. It is kept below the risk-free rate (3.5%) and nominal GDP.
driverWhy.exit: ASML's 5-yr average EV/EBITDA is ~30x (35x forward in Aug-26). 25x applies a discount because growth has decelerated by FY30. Semi-equipment peers (AMAT, LRCX, KLAC) have traded at ~18-25x.
driverWhy.wacc_adj: Bear prices extra risk for export-control and cyclical exposure. Bull assumes a lower risk premium for a structural AI capex cycle.

story.Bear: AI capex digestion in 2027-28 coincides with tighter China export controls (DUV immersion and servicing). Customers push out EUV orders, the down-payment float shrinks and margins compress as fixed R&D is held.
story.Base: 2026 guidance is delivered, the backlog converts, and EUV/High-NA adoption in logic and DRAM grows revenue to about EUR 63bn by 2030 with margins at the 2030 target band.
story.Bull: A sustained AI-driven leading-edge build-out plus faster High-NA adoption push revenue beyond the 2030 range, with gross margin at 60% and services scaling on the installed base.

milestones.title: Founded
milestones.text: Joint venture of Philips and ASM International, starting in a shed next to a Philips office in Eindhoven.

milestones.title: IPO
milestones.text: Listed on Amsterdam and Nasdaq; full independence funds the R&D race against Nikon and Canon.

milestones.title: Silicon Valley Group
milestones.text: Acquisition adds US scale and the step-and-scan know-how behind the TWINSCAN platform.

milestones.title: First EUV tool
milestones.text: The NXE:3100 pre-production EUV system ships to a customer research fab after 20+ years of R&D.

milestones.title: Customers co-invest
milestones.text: Intel, TSMC and Samsung fund EUV development and take equity stakes, which locks in the ecosystem.

milestones.title: Cymer
milestones.text: Acquiring the EUV light-source maker secures the hardest part of the EUV supply chain.

milestones.title: HMI
milestones.text: E-beam metrology joins the portfolio and extends holistic lithography beyond the scanner.

milestones.title: EUV in volume
milestones.text: The first EUV-made chips reach consumer devices; EUV becomes mandatory below 7nm.

milestones.title: High-NA
milestones.text: The first EXE:5000 High-NA EUV system ships, extending the roadmap into the 2030s.

milestones.title: Record year
milestones.text: EUR 32.7bn sales, EUR 38.8bn backlog and 48 EUV systems recognised as AI demand broadens.
